newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI resumes dollar buying, dealers puzzled.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI resumes dollar buying, dealers puzzled.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) resumed its intervention in the foreign exchange market on Wednesday after a week's absence, puzzling dealers.
"If he is coming at these levels, he must be having some concern," said a dealer about RBI's intervention at 35.73 level.
Dealers, used to RBI intervention in recent months to arrest the rupee's rise against the dollar, did not expect an intervention when the rupee was under pressure.
"It must be to safeguard exporters' interests," said one dealer. "There could be more to it, but we don't know."
An uptrend in overnight call rates also helped the rise.
Paying pressure from some clients including the Industrial Development Bank of India, India's largest long-term lending institution, also helped the premia rise, dealers said.
"With the spot (dollar) firming up, people prefer to cover," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There is also some profit-booking," she said.
